claim: WeBER reports that administrative data are still not consistently shared
problem: WeBER does not say this. Its text says the once-only principle is 'not applied consistently by service providers' and reports citizens submitting documents; the report never discusses sharing of administrative data between bodies and does not name the Bus. The wording matches the RI-TEC-028 issue definition, not the source, and it turns a citizen-side finding into a finding on data exchange, which the same case's not_transferable field says the evidence does not reach.
suggested_fix: Replace with: WeBER reports that the once-only principle is not applied consistently, with around 53 to 54% of surveyed citizens saying they had to submit documents the state already held.

claim: in_practice: WeBER, an independent monitor, confirms the once-only principle is applied in sampled services
problem: Value does not follow. The 3/3 is WeBER indicator E 1.9, the same indicator as Montenegro, where the report says points were given because documentation lists are publicly available (MNE-CSO-2025-001-0006 and the next sentence on p.22). The Serbian report gives no different basis, so nothing shows exchange observed in practice. WeBER's own conclusion is 'not applied consistently' and citizen experience scores 0.5/2. Near-identical evidence gives INT-MNE-0023 the value unclear, so the two cases are treated differently, and only the Montenegro case discloses the limit of the 3/3.
suggested_fix: Propose unclear, matching INT-MNE-0023, or say why Serbia differs. Add to CMP-0005 limitations that the 3/3 method is not shown to rest on observed exchange.

claim: mixed: providers score 3/3 on published document lists, while citizen experience scores 0/2 and the Commission says application is inconsistent
problem: Blurs implementation and outcome. The only positive side is a score the same case says rests on published lists, which is not a result. All outcome-type evidence is negative or unclear (0/2; 19.9% with an unclear base). The intervention's own status is unclear (INT-MNE-0023), and there is no baseline, so a mixed result is not supported. The link basis ('reports the survey under once-only in practice') also states no causal claim, and second-pass classification noted the item as implementation.
suggested_fix: Propose insufficient_evidence, state that the 3/3 is an implementation indicator, and reconsider whether this leads_to link should exist.

claim: conditional: fits North Macedonia on the condition that registers are digitalised in machine-readable form
problem: The item does not state a lesson. It is an oral remark by a UNDP manager, classified as a barrier, that e-services rely on registries and data exchange. It describes no mechanism tried in Montenegro and no result, and the reason itself says it explains a dependency, not what raises use. Codebook 6 asks whether the underlying mechanism could work; there is none here to transfer.
suggested_fix: Withdraw the judgement, or propose insufficient_evidence with a note that the item is context and not a lesson.

claim: Machine-translated evidence used under the comparator language limit
problem: LIM-0029 covers comparator legal texts only (reason: 'Primary law is needed'), and LIM-0012 covers Macedonian and Albanian only. The machine-translated Moldovan and Montenegrin sources here are not legal texts: an audit report, an agency web page, an implementation report and a government contribution. They carry the only independent Moldovan evidence, all Moldovan volume figures and all Montenegrin JSERP counts. This use is outside any logged limit.
suggested_fix: Raise at G6b: propose widening LIM-0029 to named non-legal sources with no English version, for the analyst to decide, and record the gap until then.

claim: The stalled inspection parallels North Macedonia's missing inspection competence, but it shows the lever was not pulled
problem: Goes further than the evidence and against the case's own judgement. The official says only that strengthening the inspection was not achieved because of staffing delays. INT-MNE-0004 says no source shows what the inspection does now or whether it has acted on data exchange. An existing but understaffed inspection is also not the same as a competence that has not been established.
suggested_fix: Say: an official reports that strengthening the inspection was not achieved; no source shows whether it has acted on data exchange, so the case says nothing on inspection as a lever.

claim: All use figures are government self-reports; Montenegro has the only use series; no independent source measures use
problem: The same RCC source the case cites gives an independent indicator of data reuse: pre-filled forms 24 (2023) to 49 (2025), defined by RCC as how far online forms reuse data already held by authorities, and described as weaker than the regional average. It is not JSERP use, and the 2025 value comes from desk research, but it is independent evidence of the kind the case says is missing. It was not in the case input because it was tagged RI-TEC-036 only.
suggested_fix: Add the item to CMP-0006 as an independent proxy, with its limits (no link to JSERP, possible break in method), and narrow the absence claim to direct measures of platform use. No cause should be inferred.

claim: a 2023 cybersecurity crisis delayed digital services
problem: The date conflicts within the evidence and the conflict is not reported. The Commission 2025 report says 2023, but its 2024 report says 'the 2022 cyber-attack' (p.25 area, source text) and the open government plan says 'the 2022 attacks'. Second-pass classification had already noted that the year conflicts.
suggested_fix: Say: a major cybersecurity crisis, dated 2023 by the Commission's 2025 report and 2022 by other sources including its 2024 report.

claim: Low: one survey with no baseline, no link to JSERP
problem: The intervention on this link is the once-only principle, not JSERP, so 'no link to JSERP' does not bear on it. The value still holds on the other grounds.
suggested_fix: Drop the JSERP phrase, or say why the principle cannot be separated from the system.

claim: The Commission says in 2024 and 2025 that ... integrating all public registers into the exchange system is incomplete
problem: The incompleteness statement is in the 2025 report only. The 2024 report recommends working towards interoperability of registers, which is a different statement.
suggested_fix: Separate the two: 2024 and 2025 on the procedure law; 2025 on register integration.

claim: The share of catalogue e-services ... was 0 in 2023 and 2024, against a 10% target
problem: Correct against the source table (p.14 and the annex), but the 10% target is not in the cited evidence item, whose text stops at 'n/a, 0, 0'.
suggested_fix: Add the target to the item by a new row, or cite the table location directly.

claim: a platform being rebuilt
problem: Out of date against the case's own reform field. 'Being developed' comes from the April 2025 report; the September 2026 text says the X-Road platform 'has been established' and equates it with JSERP.
suggested_fix: Say a platform replaced between the 2025 and 2026 texts.

claim: the only use series ... counts of connected institutions and of active exchanges can move separately
problem: Rests on two self-reported points. The later one comes from a text marked PREDLOG (proposal), which the case does not say, and an unchanged 21 alongside a 45 to 265 Metaregister jump may be a figure carried forward. The queries figure has one year only, so 'series' overstates it.
suggested_fix: Call it two reported points, disclose the proposal status, and word the lesson as 'may' and as not verified.

claim: High: closest match, Commission wording on the same procedure law and on electronic communication
problem: The reason cites no North Macedonian item, so the match cannot be checked. In the North Macedonian EU items, 'once-only' appears only in the country's own screening presentation (a reported view), so no Commission wording matches on that point. The evidence shows no underuse by connected institutions, and the case lists four differences in not_transferable.
suggested_fix: Cite the North Macedonian items compared; consider Medium, with the reason stated.

claim: No independent source addresses it
problem: A speaker from the Association of Managers at the Institute Alternative event calls the meta-register the foundation for e-services (source text; no evidence item extracted). This does not show use, so the value is unaffected, but the absence claim is too wide.
evidence_item_ids: MNE-CSO-2025-002 (source text, Tabaš remarks; no item)
suggested_fix: Say: no independent source reports its contents or use.

claim: (no statement on Institute Alternative's independence)
problem: CMP-0005 discloses that the Ministry is a WeBER project associate; CMP-0006 does not, although the Montenegrin ministry is named as project associate in the report and as co-funder in the event report, and it owns JSERP. The success and status judgements rely on this source as non-government evidence.
suggested_fix: Add the same disclosure to CMP-0006.

claim: WeBER, an independent monitor ... independent evidence
problem: CMP-0005 limitations say the Ministry is a named project associate of WeBER. The judgements call it independent without qualification, and independence is what lifts the value above 'government reporting alone'.
suggested_fix: Say a civil society monitor, with the Ministry as project associate.

claim: mixed: the principle is applied in sampled services, yet around 53% report submitting documents already held
problem: The positive side is an implementation indicator, not a result (see INT-SRB-0008). The link basis is WeBER's reading that the principle is not applied consistently, which is not a claim that the law led to this outcome. Second-pass classification noted the item as implementation, and unlike the 170 million figure this is not disclosed. Mixed can be defended only on 68% against 53% and the 0.5/2 score, but the 68% item is not cited.
suggested_fix: Rest the value on the perception items and cite them, or propose insufficient_evidence. Disclose the reclassification.

claim: WeBER's survey on documents resubmitted is not about the Bus
problem: Cited item SRB-CSO-2025-001-0001 says citizen-centric delivery is 'better regulated'. It is not the survey.
suggested_fix: Cite SRB-CSO-2025-001-0003 or 0013 in both rows.

claim: Low
problem: Inconsistent with attribution on INT-SRB-0003>SRB-GOV-2023-002-0004 and INT-MNE-0005>MNE-GOV-2025-002-0012, both insufficient_evidence because no measured outcome exists. The eEnrolment claim also has no measure, only a government statement.
suggested_fix: Apply one treatment to all unmeasured government-only outcomes.

claim: SRB-EU-2025-001-0008 and 0011 used in the case, and the Commission's fragmented responsibilities echo the coordination mechanism
problem: Second-pass classification left both items outside RI-TEC-028 on purpose ('RI-TEC-028 is not stretched to cover it'; 'does not mention data sharing'). The case hedges the wording, but it still uses 0008 to support the relevance value and lists both as implementation.
suggested_fix: Keep them as context only, drop them from the relevance reason's support, or propose reclassification at G6b.

claim: SRB-CSO-2025-001-0001 and SRB-EU-2025-001-0011 listed as implementation
problem: Both state that a legal framework or regulation exists, which is reform. SRB-EU-2024-001-0010 and 0011 are the same sentence, split between implementation and reform.
suggested_fix: Move the two legal items to reform_items and count the repeated sentence once.

claim: no source measures it
problem: True for use by institutions, but the RCC source gives Serbia a pre-filled forms score of 61 (2023) and 62 (2025), and says this shows 'potential to further ... enhance data reuse across public administration'. This independent proxy sits against 'more databases connected'. The Serbia profile was not extracted, so no item exists.
evidence_item_ids: ALB-IO-2026-001 (source text, Serbia profile; no item)
suggested_fix: Extract the rows by a new item and add them as an independent proxy, with no cause inferred.

claim: the mechanism match to coordination and resources is weak in what can be read
problem: The same audit passage restating 2020 lists 'insufficient coordination, monitoring and control' and low institutional capacity of public authorities, and the follow-up cites ineffective communication and low institutional capacity as general reasons. These are general and not about MConnect, but 'weak in what can be read' is too strong.
suggested_fix: Say coordination and capacity appear in general audit findings, not tied to platform use. Re-check the value.

claim: the audit that would show it is blocked
problem: MDA-GOV-2021-001 was never read (the register says 'title from the URL; page not read'), so it cannot be said what it would show. This also comes close to using the excerpts LIM-0028 and the case exclude.
suggested_fix: Say: the audit that might address it is blocked.

claim: a designed route for participants with no information system; the only source is a 2020 design slide; describing a design
problem: 'Designed for ... participants who do not have IS' means intended for them. The slide describes an access mode configured under Law 142/2018 and GD 211/2019, followed by a Notary Chamber case study on slides 18 to 20, so it is not shown to be only a design. INT-MDA-0032 is the date.gov.md portal, but its reason judges the route and not the portal, and Interoperable Europe describes the portal as existing. The case also says the route speaks to 'the same barrier' as North Macedonia's lack of communications software, but having no information system is not the same barrier.
suggested_fix: Describe it as an access route stated in 2020 with no later confirmation; judge the portal's status separately; say 'a related barrier'.

claim: the 2025 report asks only for stronger interoperability between verification systems and state registries; the Commission does not raise it
problem: The sentence is about asset declaration verification under Chapter 23 and is flagged theme_doubtful, which the case does not say. The 2024 report is passed over although it records 14 fragmented systems in the labour ministry 'leading to interoperability ... challenges', and the 2025 report says 'access and use of digital public services significantly increased', which bears on use on the citizen side. It is true that neither names MConnect. The search list in evidence_of_results also omits the sources that report service use, MDA-CSO-2023-001 and MDA-GOV-2024-002.
suggested_fix: State the Chapter 23 context, add the 2024 item, and widen the search list. The 'no outcome evidence' claim otherwise holds for the 2021 amendments and for use by institutions.

claim: MDA-GOV-2024-001-0004 and 0005 listed as implementation
problem: Both restate the 2020 audit, adopted in December 2020, before the amendments took effect on 18 January 2021. They describe the problem and cannot show how the reform was implemented. MDA-IO-2024-002-0005 ('on the right track') and MDA-EU-2025-001-0001 are also not implementation of this reform.
suggested_fix: Move them to context or the problem field.

claim: Interoperable Europe and the agency state that Law 142/2018 defines data exchange through MConnect
problem: The agency item cited (0005) gives only the effective date of the amendments. MDA-GOV-2021-002-0002 is the item naming the law, and the 'defines' wording is Interoperable Europe's alone.
suggested_fix: Cite 0002 and attribute 'defines' to Interoperable Europe only.

claim: The Code is in force and was amended, effective 18 January 2021
problem: The only cited item does not name the Code. MDA-GOV-2021-002-0003 does.

claim: a duty on officials and bodies backed by a personal sanction, could be written into comparable administrative law
problem: Being able to write the sanction into law is not transferability of a working mechanism, and no item in this case has a transferability judgement. The case-level text therefore rests on no judged lesson, although the practical lesson is careful.
suggested_fix: Say the wording could be copied but the case gives no evidence that it would raise use; say no item states a lesson.

claim: conditional: it could apply if a body has the competence to monitor, which its strategy says is not established for ICT laws
problem: The item is a finding that states a need, not a tested lesson, as the reason admits. The condition also does not fit: WeBER means monitoring the quality and legal compliance of service delivery, while MKD-GOV-2023-002-0029 concerns inspection of laws on ICT use. A gap in ICT inspection says little about monitoring compliance with the procedure law.
suggested_fix: Mark it as a stated need, not a lesson, and state a condition on monitoring compliance with the Law on General Administrative Procedure, or use insufficient_evidence.

claim: unlikely
problem: The item is a recommendation to Serbian bodies, inferred from a survey, not a lesson from something tried. The value is a fair reading of fit, but the record should say so. No North Macedonian evidence on citizen awareness is cited, so 'would not reach them' is the agent's inference.
suggested_fix: Note that it is a recommendation with no tested mechanism.
